title: slab-evict-coordinator-frag-oscillation-fix-and-hosted-dedupe-mitigation
creator: Sarah Kim
description:
Summary: Customer-facing spike in GPU OOMs across mixed-hosted and Dedicated pools traced to eviction-coordinator oscillation combined with uneven KV-cache tombstone distribution. Symptoms included periodic OOM waves, long tail latency, and scattered session failures. Goal: stabilize allocation under mixed latency/throughput workloads by introducing a soft-slab headroom policy, deterministic tombstone sweeping, and an emergency throttling knob for hosted bursts without regressing tail latency for dedicated tenants.

Investigation notes:
- Incident timeline: first escalations received 2025-10-28; repeat patterns every 12–18 hours.
- Root cause hypothesis: eviction coordinator would trigger aggressive slab reclamation in response to transient high-throughput phases. That reclamation left small, non-contiguous free regions which increased fragmentation and prevented large contiguous allocations for KV cache growth, finally causing OOMs. Simultaneously, tombstone accumulation in the KV index caused allocation hotspots on a subset of arenas.
- Repro: synthetic workload reproducer created (load-mix: 60% short-chat, 30% long-context generation, 10% embedding backfills) reproduces fragmentation + OOM on scale testbed (2x dedicated-GPU nodes) with seed config.

Solution implemented (high level):
1) Soft-slab headroom: allocator now maintains a soft threshold per-slab type (based on median request peak for tenant) which prevents complete reclamation below threshold and allows small transient expansion without compaction; reduces oscillation.
2) Reactive compaction backoff: eviction coordinator now uses a rate-limited compaction window and prefers contiguous-slab consolidation instead of atomized frees under high churn.
3) Tombstone sweeper: background KV index sweeper runs incremental passes using lightweight sampling to prevent index hotspots; tombstone compaction deferred to low-load windows and bounded by IOPS to avoid interfering with latency SLOs.
4) Emergency throttles: hosted burst throttle added to control concurrent prefetch/evict work for shared pools; dedicated tenants keep priority path preserved. Throttle knob exposed via console flags for SRE during escalations.
5) Telemetry & alerts: new metrics (slab_fragmentation_ratio, kv_tombstone_rate_by_arena, eviction_burst_rate) and an alert runbook created.

Rollback/compatibility: change is backwards compatible. Soft-thresholds default to conservative values; flagging available for rapid tuning.

QA & testing: unit tests for allocator invariants added; integration stress test harness extended to include tombstone-heavy index patterns. Long-running soak tests passed on staging (72h) with previous failing repro workload.

Customer communication: coordinated incident post noting mitigations, ETA for non-urgent follow-ups, and recommended tenant-level knobs for customers running large embedding backfills.
